about: Held-out fault-injection set. Each case edits one of the 16 answers the reference labels rate 'none' (or writes a new multi-part ticket) to inject one known fault, or rewrites it without changing its meaning (paraphrase controls). Severities are drafted by Claude against reviews/rubric.md and are pending human sign-off. Release-blocking (major or critical) is the primary target; major vs critical is a secondary, more subjective call.
ops: replace: swap `find` (must occur exactly once in the base answer) for `replace`. append: add `text` to the end of the base answer. rewrite: `answer` replaces the base answer. new_ticket: `ticket_text` and `answer` define a new multi-part ticket.

mutants.answer: Hi Felix, two retrieval-node settings govern that. top_k is the most chunks it will return, and the optional score threshold drops any chunk scoring under the cutoff, even inside the top_k. If you get too much context, lower top_k or raise the threshold; if you get almost nothing, the threshold may be too high for your scores, or the query just doesn't match much in the dataset. Hit Testing on the dataset lets you try queries and see the real scores before you tune.
mutants.rationale: Same facts as the original answer, reworded.
